payload.claim: The `EXHAUSTED` branch restates `_next_state`'s own merge check (`pr.get("state") == "MERGED"`) instead of calling `_next_state(pr)` and testing its result for `"MERGED"`. The two copies agree today, but this is a duplicated helper rather than an imported one, and it is the reason the spec's own criterion-1 mutant (which edits the `if state == "MERGED":` line inside `_next_state`, saffron/reconcile.py:125) has no effect on this code path: an `EXHAUSTED` row never reaches `_next_state` at all. The result is that the acceptance criterion this line implements is not actually pinned by the mutant the spec declares for it (witness gate: '1 of 3 witness(es) survived their own mutant'), even though calling `_next_state` and filtering its return for `"MERGED"` would have produced identical behaviour while keeping the merge-detection logic in one place.
